title: What to pack for a winter Spiti departure
excerpt: Layers, a decent headlamp, and the things people always forget once the bus leaves Shimla.
body:
Winter Spiti is cold in a dry, precise way. You do not need expedition gear. You need a system you can add and remove while the vehicle climbs.

Start with a warm base layer, a fleece, and a wind shell. The shell matters more than a heavy jacket during the day, because the sun is strong and the wind is stronger. Evenings want the heavy layer, a wool cap, and gloves you can still use a phone with.

Pack socks you trust, a small pharmacy, and copies of your ID. Lip balm is not a luxury above Tabo. If you bring one extra thing, make it a power bank — outlets in homestays are shared, and the group chat is how we confirm the next morning's start.
author: Pack my bags desk

title: How to choose your first group trip
excerpt: Duration, altitude, and the kind of evening you actually want after a long day.
body:
The right first group trip is the one you will finish glad, not the one with the most dramatic photograph.

If you have never slept above 3,000 metres, start with Meghalaya, Kerala, or a long-weekend trek that comes back down each night. Ladakh and winter Spiti are wonderful, and they are also a poor place to discover that you hate early mornings and shared bathrooms at the same time.

Read the itinerary for rest, not just sights. A good departure has at least one unscheduled evening. Ask who the captain is, how big the group gets, and whether the price includes the boring essentials: permits, breakfast, and the vehicle that waits when someone needs ten more minutes.
author: Meera Iyer

title: Kerala in October, without the checklist
excerpt: The rains are thinning, the backwaters are full, and the beach is better in the evening than at noon.
body:
October in Kerala is a shoulder month, which is exactly why we like it. The landscape is green, the houseboats are easier to book, and the midday sun has not turned cruel yet.

Plan the hills before the coast. Munnar in the morning, a houseboat that boards before lunch, and Varkala only once you are ready to stop moving. Carry a light rain jacket anyway. The season does not owe you a dry afternoon.

Eat the fish. Skip the shops that meet the bus. And if the group wants a free evening, take it — Kerala is one of the few circuits that gets better when you remove an activity.
author: Pack my bags desk

title: International weeks that fit a work calendar
excerpt: Vietnam, Bali, and Almaty are the departures we recommend when someone has exactly seven days.
body:
A week is enough if the route refuses to be greedy. That is the whole trick.

Vietnam north-to-central works because the internal flight does the hard kilometre. Bali with the Gilis works because the boat is booked and the free day is real. Almaty works because the mountains are an hour from a city you can land in at night and still enjoy the next morning.

What does not work is a seven-day plan with four cities and a shopping stop. If a colleague asks for Dubai and a desert and a theme park and a second emirate, tell them to take ten days or pick one mood. Pack my bags’ international calendar is built around one mood per departure.
author: Arun Deshpande
